gap: No result ChatGPT got works out the yearly energy the inverter burns just by being switched on (idle W × 8,760 h): about 788 kWh/yr for the Sol-Ark 15K, 613 kWh/yr for the EG4 18kPV, 438 kWh/yr for the EG4 6000XP and 70 kWh/yr for the Schneider XW Pro 6848. None works the 18kPV's daily idle draw (1.68 kWh) out as about 12% of a 14.3 kWh battery.
standout_why: I compared against the cited ecosolarkits.com/blogs/guides/eg4-vs-sol-ark, solar-electric.com's buying guide and solargearscout.com/guides/off-grid-vs-hybrid-inverter, plus the top uncited results liveoffthegrid.com/specs/inverters and wildjoule.com (best hybrid inverter, best off-grid inverter). Ecosolarkits already lists battery-only cost per kW. Liveoffthegrid already shows idle W × 24 = Wh/day and cost per kW for 10 split-phase models. Wildjoule states 1.7 kWh/day for the 18kPV and 1.2 kWh/day for the 6000XP. What's missing everywhere: yearly idle energy, idle as a share of a battery bank, and a fix for liveoffthegrid's Sol-Ark 15K cost per kW, which divides by the 15 kW PV-assisted rating instead of the 12 kW battery-only rating. That fix moves it from $383 to $479 per kW. These add to the rivals' figures but don't give the page a new fact.
decides: It backs the EG4 18kPV as the value pick for whole-home hybrid use: about $333–$408 per battery-only kW against the Sol-Ark 15K's $471–$479, and it idles 20 W lower (613 vs 788 kWh/yr). For off-grid cabins the EG4 6000XP is cheapest per kW ($250). The Schneider XW Pro costs the most per kW ($544) but wastes about 1/9 the 18kPV's idle energy, about 1/11 the Sol-Ark 15K's and about 1/6 the 6000XP's. That matters on a small battery with little winter sun. Dealectric's own Sun Gold Power 6000W unit is cheap at $203/kW but has no MPPT, so it needs a separate solar charge controller, and every variant showed as sold out on 2026-11-10.
